rationale: Round 3 plan (replaces round 2's 6 copies per plate). Stock 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3 + Prusament PETG (filament_type PETG = print_requirements; 250 °C, first layer 240, bed 90/85, fan 30-50 %: inside 230-250 / 80-90 and the skill's PETG range, so not overridden). Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly as strength modelled the femur: 4 perimeters (1.67 mm band), 5 top / 5 bottom layers (1.0 mm skins), 50 % gyroid, 0.2 mm layers. Elephant-foot 0.2 pairs with the 0.4 mm bed chamfer; the bed face carries the horn pocket and, reversed, the tibia servo's tabs, so it must print true. Copies 3, the same file printed on 2 plates = spec §7 (6 femurs, 3 h per batch; sliced 2.07 h): round 2's 6 per plate took 3.93 h, over the limit. The brief's 4 + 2 would need two different G-code files, and a job holds one part.gcode, so 3 + 3 prints the same approved file twice. Orientation is in the STL (brief): flat, horn pocket on the bed. No library rows (materials.csv and lessons.md are empty), so no flow, temperature or xy compensation overrides. Seam: aligned (stated explicitly), which keeps seams in corners and holes, off the window's 0.1 mm end-clearance faces (random would scatter them there). Checked in the G-code: the outline's seam is at the hub end (x -7, y -6.4), the window's in its inboard +y corner (27.9, 6.4), the rest in the pilots, the tie slot, the clamp hole and the horn pocket's arm tip. None is at a governing section (the nearest, the inner pilot row at x 25.6, has SF 8.9 or more in XY), so staggered inner seams are not needed. Brim: none (brim_width 0): PETG barely warps on a 7 mm flat plate, and a brim would fill the 0.4 mm bed chamfer and leave a lip on the bed face, which carries the tibia servo's tabs.
